subject: Passing Data, in an R package, which includes javascript

messages.author: 84069de49fcefd1b
messages.subject: Passing Data, in an R package, which includes javascript
parts:
Hi everybody,

I'd like to build a nice shiny app to interactively display data in my R package. My problem is, how do I get the users data in the app.

Say I have a data.frame X and I'd like the R user to just use a function from my package, say display(X) for which he will then have a full shiny app to visualize and play with the data.

In order to do this, I believe I have three solutions: 
  • Either make X a global variable so that the code which is in ui.R and server.R of my "inst" directory will see X (or any new global variable name I'd like it to be) when I call shiny::runApp(system.file("myPackageName",package="CoRegNet")
  • Or write X in a generic file, I guess in the inst directory again, and have a global.R file to always read the same file as input data
  • Or have all the ui.R and server.R code in a list that can be the parameter of the runApp function.

Obviously, the two first solution are kind of ugly, read/write data between two R scripts just sounds silly and I'm not really comfortable with using global variable. 

The third solution just sounds great then. The problem is, I have a javascript file to include, which of course is now in a www folder of the inst of my package and I have no idea how to include it.

If anyone has any idea, that would simply be great.

Cheers,

Remy

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Passing Data, in an R package, which includes javascript
parts:
I think you can put your JS file under inst/ in your package, and use

includeScript(system.file('path/to/your.js', package = 'CoRegNet'))

Regards,
Yihui
